headline: MoEZip reports stronger task scores under aggressive KV-cache compression in tested sparse language models
summary: An arXiv paper proposes MoEZip, which uses router Fisher-trace sensitivity and attention to retain context positions intended to stabilize expert routing during KV-cache eviction. In author-run comparisons, it reports higher long-context benchmark scores than KVZip, SnapKV and PyramidKV at high compression on Qwen3 and GLM-4.7-Flash sparse models. In a Qwen3-235B-A22B appendix, the authors report a 10-task LongBench macro of 44.7 versus 27.6 for KVZip at 10% KV retention. The authors also estimate 15,000–16,000 A100 GPU-hours for MoEZip and all baselines together, excluding preliminary or failed runs. The reported benchmark results have not been independently reproduced; Appendix C says code is in supplementary material, which this activation did not retrieve, while the linked repository page lists only a README and license.
